title: Sprints 6j to 6l: a project with its developer — Laptop, VM A and VM B

steps.say:
On the Laptop, 0-1. What this pass needs. The Laptop is the operator's own computer and the host admin: rent, prepare, its installation VPN, admit walkadmin, register, take off, lock, purge and give back. Every host, Core and Matrix check and both gathered-push invocations run here in Claude Code as ! bash …. The Laptop also creates the private GitHub repositories; VM A seeds them as walkadmin.

VM A is the Ubuntu 26.04 libvirt VM walk-laptop-c at 192.168.122.245. Its existing desktop account is walkadmin (uid 1000, sudo), the project admin, whose host laptop name is walklaptop at 10.73.<n>.3. Make records this account and preserves its password and sudo; removal keeps the account. VM B is test-ubuntu-vm, 192.168.122.174, with its console and original login; the walk creates walkdev. VM A and VM B both run laptop-b-*.sh; the Laptop runs laptop-a-repositories.sh, and VM A runs laptop-a-seed.sh. Those file names stay as written. Keep both VMs isolated from concurrent VPN/internal-host changes until cleanup.

Host: walk6. Project: walk6-demo. Allow about 90 minutes (a guess), including the host guide's approximately 20 minutes of checks and Core/Matrix's approximately 5 minutes each. One server with its forge is rented and given back. This pass still uses the per-person VPNs while normal work moves to ssh alone.

On the Laptop have the Scaleway key/project UUID, rental SSH pair, sudo password, ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx and master password; GitHub credentials for the private repositories porelo-ai/walk6-demo and porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access. The operator's token has Contents write and Administration on exactly those two. VM A uses the same operator GitHub account and token rights, entered separately in Git's in-memory helper and Your forges; its signing key is its own, generated on VM A before seed, and seeds there with that protected key in its agent. project.yml lists walkadmin's public line alone; this same line is carried to the Laptop for registration and to VM B for verification. No operator signing key is needed. VM B uses the developer's actual GitHub test-account login/token and accepts both read invitations.

The Laptop needs Flutter/Dart from pubspec.yaml, Linux desktop build tools, a working local Porelo and unlocked secret store, Bash, git, ssh, scp, ssh-keygen, curl, jq, python3, python3-yaml, sha256sum, wg, wg-quick, keepassxc-cli, sudo, ip, ping, openssl and update-ca-certificates. Both VMs need a desktop secret store, Bash, git, python3, ssh, scp, ssh-keygen, wg, wg-quick, keepassxc-cli, sudo, update-ca-certificates and the Linux system tools checked by join: sh, ip, ping, cat, install, date, sleep, awk, cmp, mktemp, chmod, mv, rm, grep, head, tail, sed, base64, id, stat and mkdir. Make also needs apt-get, dpkg-deb, useradd, usermod and passwd, plus dpkg-repack if replacing installed Porelo; start needs tar and pgrep. Porelo comes from the handover. Ansible runs on the host.

Keep porelo-host doc/guides/6-host.md at 107f786 and its 13 scripts in ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/6/ beside you, including 6-host-push-run.sh. Core: ~/.porelo/handover/porelo/6-pass/porelo-checks.md; Matrix: ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-message-matrix/6-pass/6-matrix.md. Verify intended host snapshots before starting: Core 3c5b5eff or later and Matrix 982e063 or later; keep them stable. The collection is ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/2443282/porelo-host-0.5.9-snapshot.tar.gz, SHA-256 005fcd24363aebcac123e6d50df5dc8510461d7a2576ea240baac3d0ac32913e.

Both VMs receive ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-frontend/walk23/ from the Laptop. It holds the debug bundle, shared VM scripts, laptop-a-seed.sh, porelo_0.5.1~snapshot.900+local.20261029T192331_amd64.deb, SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.sha256. The last file holds <walk23-digest>, kept symbolic here and read with cat on the Laptop. The interface bundle must include the join fix 2a79f67, which removes prior secrets-file selection; do not substitute this worktree's older unchanged lib files. The bundle must include the published bring wizard from 93651c9 and the hand-over/start/make/remove scripts from 9794174. VM A creates its encrypted secrets file before bring in step 5-4; the wizard chooses that existing file.

Expected: (not run) all three machines and artifacts are identified, VM A owns its signing private key, and its sole public signer is used for seed, host registration, bring and Developers. Failure signs: unprepared handover transfer, missing tool/snapshot, wrong digest, an older join bundle or an older bring bundle. No live step is rehearsed. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 0-2. In a separate terminal in your own login, read the manifest's digest (not run):

cat ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-frontend/walk23/SHA256SUMS.sha256

Keep it as <walk23-digest>. Copy the complete folder to VM B using its existing VM account, replacing the account placeholder; /var/tmp/walk23 must not already exist (not run):

scp -r ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-frontend/walk23 <vm-b-original-account>@192.168.122.174:/var/tmp/walk23

VM A's walkadmin SSH account takes keys only. Copy the same folder to its /var/tmp/walk23 through the VM console's file-transfer facility, or with an SSH key the operator adds through that console. The available console transfer facility/key installation has not been verified: this is a preparation gap. Do not try password scp or assume a key exists. Once the operator has added and tested a key, this conditional command from the Laptop copies it (not run):

scp -r ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-frontend/walk23 walkadmin@192.168.122.245:/var/tmp/

In each VM's console, make the public handover readable/traversable (not run):

chmod -R a+rX /var/tmp/walk23

Read its manifest's digest and compare with the Laptop (not run):

sha256sum /var/tmp/walk23/SHA256SUMS

In a separate terminal whose working directory is /var/tmp/walk23 on each VM, verify every file, including laptop-a-seed.sh (not run):

sha256sum --check --strict SHA256SUMS

Expected: (not run; VM A transfer method pending) both digests match, every listed file says OK, and walkdev/walkadmin can read the handover. Failure signs: no console transfer or tested SSH key, digest mismatch, unreadable file or nested walk23 directory. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on after both copies are verified.

On the Laptop, 0-3. VM A's existing walkadmin password is held only in /home/michi/.porelo/keys/walk-laptop-c-walkadmin.password, mode 0600. Read it privately on the Laptop outside Claude Code, terminal recording, logs and this panel; never paste it here or print it into an agent session. Use it at VM A's console login and sudo prompts. Its SSH account accepts keys only; this password does not enable the transfer in step 0-2. Expected: (not run) walkadmin's existing password is available privately and its existing sudo membership is kept. Failure signs: missing/unreadable password file, broader permissions or password exposed in a transcript. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 0-4. Start the interface from ~/git/porelo-frontend in a separate terminal that stays open (not run):

bash tool/start_host_walk.sh --visible --roles host-admin 23 ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/2443282

Expected: (not run) the collection matches its manifest, the Linux debug bundle opens with the host-admin role and this panel is visible. Failure signs: start-host-walk: step 0-1 failed, missing role commands or a build failure. Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-5. In the console, log into the existing walkadmin desktop account (uid 1000, sudo). In its separate terminal run (not run):

sudo PORELO_WALK_DEVELOPER=walkadmin bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-b-make.sh <walk23-digest>

Type walkadmin's existing sudo password, read privately on the Laptop in step 0-3. Do not change it. Expected: (not run) make records that walkadmin and sudo already exist, keeps the password and account, installs the verified package and saves a previous Porelo package if needed; laptop-b-make passed. Failure signs: digest/package mismatch, missing prerequisite, a password-reset prompt or a before-state claiming the account was newly made. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-6. Log into the console as walkadmin. Before VM A runs seed, generate walkadmin's own signing key in a separate terminal. Use a passphrase-protected key and a dedicated SSH agent: the private file stays encrypted on VM A, and Git's requested .pub configuration uses the loaded key without repeated GUI prompts. Never copy the private key. Run each command in order (not run); stop for existing keys and never approve an overwrite:

mkdir -p ~/.ssh

chmod 700 ~/.ssh

test ! -e ~/.ssh/walk6-signing

test ! -e ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub

ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C '' -f ~/.ssh/walk6-signing

Choose and repeat a new test-only key passphrase at ssh-keygen's prompts. Rewrite its public file without a comment or trailing space (not run), typing that passphrase when asked:

ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/walk6-signing > ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub
 Start the account's dedicated test agent and load that key (not run):

eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"

ssh-add ~/.ssh/walk6-signing

At ssh-add's prompt type the same key passphrase. Configure Git (not run):

git config --global gpg.format ssh

git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub

git config --global commit.gpgsign true

git config --global user.name 'Walk project admin'

git config --global user.email walkadmin@example.org

Print only its comment-free public line (not run):

awk '{print $1, $2}' ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub

Carry that public line only to the Laptop for registration at step 5-2 and to VM B for follow/join. VM A's seed reads this same file from Git's user.signingkey; it accepts one comment-free ssh-ed25519 line alone. Keep this terminal open for the next step: the interface must inherit its SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Expected: (not run) ssh-add confirms the key was loaded, Git selects the public file and the private half remains only on VM A. Failure signs: no agent, key not loaded, wrong passphrase, wrong key type or private data copied. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-7. In the same walkadmin terminal used for the signing-agent setup in step 0-6, enable the account’s daemon (not run):

systemctl --user enable --now porelod

Check it (not run):

systemctl --user is-active porelod

Then start the desktop interface from this same terminal, so it inherits the loaded signing agent, using the shared handover (not run):

PORELO_WALK_DEVELOPER=walkadmin PORELO_WALK_ROLES=project-admin bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-b-start.sh <walk23-digest>

Expected: (not run) active is printed and VM A's interface starts with project-admin, with no host-admin actions. Failure signs: failed unit, checksum refusal, no desktop or role error. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 0-8. In the title bar click Copy my public keys for a host…. In Copy my public keys for a host, type walk6 into Host name, then Copy my public keys. Check Public keys for walk6 copied., then Close. Carry this YAML's public ssh_public_key and wireguard_public_key to the Laptop: type the two public lines there, or save them with a text editor on VM A as /tmp/walkadmin-public.yml, then make that public-only file readable (not run):

chmod 644 /tmp/walkadmin-public.yml

Type the public text on the Laptop, or transfer this public-only file through the console method established at step 0-2. A Laptop scp from walkadmin@192.168.122.245 is available only after the operator has added and tested a key; no password SSH is assumed. Expected: (not run) VM A's per-host private halves stay in walkadmin's secret store, while the Laptop receives only the two public fields. Failure signs: wrong host, extra/private fields, secret-store refusal or changed public text. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 1-1. In a separate terminal in your own login, from ~/git/porelo-frontend, run (not run):

bash tool/walk23/laptop-a-repositories.sh

At Developer GitHub login, type the developer test account's actual GitHub login. Alternatively set PORELO_GUIDE_DEVELOPER_LOGIN before running; an explicitly empty value skips the optional invitation, which this pass needs. At the hidden GitHub token prompt, type the operator's token for exactly porelo-ai/walk6-demo and porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access and Enter. It needs repository Administration for creation/invitations; your separate Git credentials need Contents write for seeding and later gathered pushes. Expected: (not run) both repositories are private and the developer is granted/invited read access (permission pull) to walk6-demo only; laptop-a-repositories passed. The access repository's developer invitation belongs to Developers later. Failure signs: a public repository, invalid login, a login with existing stronger access, or an API refusal. Return to this panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 1-2. The repository-creation script's hidden token prompt does not fill Git's credential helper. The Laptop needs its own publishing credential for laptop-prepare and both gathered-push runners. In a separate terminal in your own account configure an in-memory helper (not run):

git config --global credential.helper 'cache --timeout=7200'

Read the private project repository (not run):

git ls-remote https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git HEAD

At Username type the operator's actual GitHub login; at Password type the operator's token restricted to the two walk repositories, with Contents write and Administration on both. Git keeps it in memory, separately from the API script and VM A's helper. The unseeded repository may print no HEAD hash; require a successful read without an authentication error. laptop-prepare later checks this access without prompting. Expected: (not run) the Laptop's helper can supply its own publishing credential during the pass; the token is not placed in an argument, file or log. Failure signs: wrong account/token, authentication refusal or a later noninteractive helper lookup failure; repeat this step if the two-hour cache expires. Return to the panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 1-3. walkadmin uses the operator's own GitHub account as project admin, with a token restricted to porelo-ai/walk6-demo and porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access and Contents write plus Administration on both. It is separate from VM B's developer login. In walkadmin's separate terminal configure Git's in-memory helper (not run):

git config --global credential.helper 'cache --timeout=7200'

Read the two private repositories (not run):

git ls-remote https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo.git HEAD

git ls-remote https://github.com/porelo-ai/walk6-demo-access.git HEAD

At Username type the operator's actual GitHub login; at Password type that restricted token. The helper keeps it in memory. The second command reuses it. VM A's sole Git signing key is ~/.ssh/walk6-signing.pub from step 0-6, with its protected private key in the dedicated agent. The secrets file is prepared at bring's own Your secrets file step. These repository reads happen before seed, so an empty repository may print no HEAD hash while still exiting successfully; stop on any authentication error. Expected: (not run) both private remotes are readable and no token is written to a file/log or argument. Failure signs: credentials/invitations refused, wrong GitHub account or copied private key. Next in the panel moves on.

On VM A, 1-4. After laptop-a-repositories.sh on the Laptop and VM A's Git credentials in step 1-3, close VM A's interface and return to its original signing/start terminal from step 0-6, which still has the dedicated SSH_AUTH_SOCK and loaded signing key. Run as walkadmin (not run):

bash /var/tmp/walk23/laptop-a-seed.sh

The script reads git's user.signingkey, requires exactly one comment-free ssh-ed25519 public line, and lists that line alone in project.yml. The protected private key in walkadmin's agent signs both initial commits. Git's in-memory helper supplies the operator's GitHub token; no private signing key is copied. project.yml names guarded, its image/repository, the private access repository and a Matrix peer; access.yml starts with developers: {}, with host and Matrix settings written by bring. Both remotes are checked before either is published. An identical signed seed is kept; different content is refused. Expected: (not run) both signed main hashes are read back and laptop-a-seed passed, with walkadmin's sole public signer. Failure signs: missing/malformed/commented user.signingkey, absent agent/key, signing or credential refusal, different content or push refusal. Restart VM A's interface from this same terminal with step 0-7's start command after seed passes. Return to the Laptop's panel; Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 1-5. In your own account, in Claude Code, run the check for 6-host.md, laptop-prepare:

! bash ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/6/6-host-laptop-prepare.sh

Expected: (not run) tools, host and Matrix manifests, GitHub read access and the collection pass; laptop-prepare passed is printed. Failure signs: a missing tool, checksum mismatch or GitHub read refusal; creation and seeding have already completed. Record a finding by its step name; return to this panel afterward. Next in the panel moves on, including when the check was already done.

On the Laptop, 2-1. In the interface: click Prepare a server… in the title bar, the server icon right of Watch another machine…. Expected: (not run) the wizard Prepare a server opens at Step 1 of 7 — Where it is rented, showing Scaleway project id and Set Scaleway key, with no Account on the server field. Failure signs: no server icon in the title bar (--roles host-admin was omitted at startup), or its tooltip reads Prepare a server… with a reason after it (keepassxc-cli is missing).

On the Laptop, 2-2. In the interface (Step 1 of 7 — Where it is rented): type your Scaleway project UUID into Scaleway project id (if your Scaleway key is not stored yet, click Set Scaleway key first and enter it in its terminal), then click Next. Expected: (not run) the Scaleway key check succeeds and Step 2 of 7 — Your server opens, proposing the lowest unused network number <n> (such as 0) with Run a forge on this server turned on; no project step is shown. Failure signs: Copy the project id from Scaleway Project, Settings. below Next, or a Scaleway key error keeping the wizard on Step 1.

On the Laptop, 2-3. In the interface (Step 2 of 7 — Your server): type walk6 into Server name, keep the proposed integer <n> in Network number (0–255) (note <n> for the 10.73.<n>.0/24 and porelo-<n> checks below), leave Run a forge on this server turned on, and click Next. Expected: (not run) Step 3 of 7 — Your ssh keys opens. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with This laptop already knows a host with that name or network. Choose another. or The server name needs one DNS label….

steps.say: On the Laptop, 2-4. In the interface (Step 3 of 7 — Your ssh keys): enter your rental SSH private key path (such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) in Your private ssh key, confirm Your public ssh key holds the matching .pub path with a check mark, and click Next. Expected: (not run) Step 4 of 7 — Your secrets file opens with ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx in Your secrets file (.kdbx), It is there: setup opens it with its master password., and Open it now. Failure signs: a refusal on Your public ssh key saying the pair does not match, or a missing key file keeping Next disabled.

On the Laptop, 2-5. In the interface (Step 4 of 7 — Your secrets file): confirm ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx is in Your secrets file (.kdbx), click Open it now, type the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx into the terminal and press Enter, then click Done. Expected: (not run) nothing you type is shown; keepassxc-cli records hosts/walk6/wireguard in ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx and the terminal prints The secrets file is ready.; after Done, the step shows Ready: the file keeps the server’s keys. Failure signs: did not open with that password; type it again., or The secrets file was not opened, so setup did not start.

On the Laptop, 2-6. In the interface (Step 4 to Step 5 of 7 — the Laptop test collection, shown in a development build): click Next, type /home/<you>/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/2443282/porelo-host-0.5.9-snapshot.tar.gz (your home in place of /home/<you>) into Test collection (.tar.gz) and 005fcd24363aebcac123e6d50df5dc8510461d7a2576ea240baac3d0ac32913e into Test collection SHA-256, then click Next. Expected: (not run) Step 6 of 7 — Check and start opens with the summary Scaleway project id: …, Server: walk6, Network: 10.73.<n>.0/24, Forge: on, No project or project account is created., your SSH keys, Secrets file: ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx, and the test collection, plus the button Prepare the server. Failure signs: Give the test collection SHA-256 as 64 hexadecimal digits. or The test collection does not exist….

On the Laptop, 2-7. In the interface (Step 6 of 7 — Check and start): verify every line of the summary, then click Prepare the server — from here on a server is rented — and when Step 7 of 7 — Preparing the server pauses at its stop, click Complete setup on the host. Expected: (not run) porelo-host up runs with --host-name walk6 --network <n> --login-user root --forge true and no project bundle or project account, then pauses waiting for you; Complete setup on walk6 opens asking only for the host's VPN key and its forge's certificate from your secrets file (no vault passphrase, no vault entries, no Tresorit login, no Matrix token). Failure signs: a refused step in the protocol, or Complete setup on walk6 asking for any secret other than wireguard and forge-certificate.

On the Laptop, 2-8. In the interface (Complete setup on walk6): click Open the terminal, type only the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx once into the terminal and press Enter (nothing else is asked), then click Done. Expected: (not run) nothing you type is shown; a lasting CA for walk6 is stored in ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx under hosts/walk6/forge-ca-key and hosts/walk6/forge-ca (constrained to walk6.porelo.internal and 10.73.<n>.0/24), certificates for forge.walk6.porelo.internal and matrix.walk6.porelo.internal are signed locally, wireguard and forge-certificate are piped to porelo-host-stop --stdin, and the terminal says The host has what it needs; setup goes on.; Done closes the stop dialog and resumes up. Failure signs: has no entry hosts/walk6/wireguard; nothing was sent., The host's certificates could not be signed; nothing was sent., or Host setup ended with code 64: a wrong call.

On the Laptop, 2-9. In the interface: wait for up to end ready (up checked in the protocol, and For the project admins shown below it). When Bring the VPN up for walk6 opens by itself, click Cancel it twice and click Finish so step 3-1 brings the VPN up from walk6's row in Machines (if you already typed your sudo password there, click Finish and go on). Then click Next in this panel. Expected: (not run) up ends ready with host.json checked. Failure signs: host.json is missing from the completed server setup. or a host.json mismatch in the protocol.

On the Laptop, 3-1. In the interface: in the rail click Machines. On walk6's row, which says In preparation, click Open the host protocol and in it click Bring the VPN up — or, if walk6 already shows as Prepared, click its chevron (Show more), open its menu (⋮), run Take the VPN down with your sudo password, then open its menu (⋮) again and click Bring the VPN up to exercise the machine row's VPN command. Type only your sudo password into Bring the VPN up for walk6 and press Enter, verify the tunnel on the Laptop, then come back here. Expected: (not run) the terminal installs porelo-<n>, confirms a fresh WireGuard handshake, trusts walk6's CA and writes forge.walk6.porelo.internal and matrix.walk6.porelo.internal into /etc/hosts; walk6 stands in Machines as Prepared. In a separate terminal on the Laptop, ip -br addr show porelo-<n> shows 10.73.<n>.2/32 and ping -c 1 10.73.<n>.1 answers (not run). Failure signs: The VPN check did not confirm this server., snap confinement, a network collision, walk6 staying in preparation or no reply. Next in the panel moves on.

On the Laptop, 3-2. In your own account, in Claude Code, run the check for 6-host.md, host-prepare:

! bash ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-host/6/6-host-prepare.sh

Expected: (not run) host.json matches, no people or projects exist, forge and homeserver answer 200, helpers and the sync sudo rule exist; host-prepare passed. Failure signs: any expected: / got: mismatch, a nonzero exit, or the named passed line missing. Record a finding by its step name; return to this panel afterward. Next in the panel moves on, including when the check was already done.

On the Laptop, 3-3. In your own account, in Claude Code, run the check for 6-matrix.md, matrix-prepare, after host-prepare:

! bash ~/.porelo/handover/porelo-message-matrix/6-pass/6-matrix-host-prepare.sh

Next in the panel moves on, including when the check was already done.

On the Laptop, 3-4. In the interface: on walk6's row in Machines, click its chevron (Show more) if closed, open its menu (⋮) (or machine-menu on walk6's own page), and click For the project admins…. Expected: (not run) the dialog For the project admins opens. Failure signs: For the project admins… is unavailable (complete the server setup first) or missing (--roles host-admin omitted).

On the Laptop, 4-1. In the interface: open walk6's menu (⋮) and click Admit a project admin…. In Step 1 of 4 — Project admin account, type walkadmin and click Next. Expected: (not run) the wizard Admit a project admin opens and advances to Step 2 of 4 — Laptop public keys. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with Use a name starting with a lower-case letter….

On the Laptop, 4-2. In Step 2 of 4 — Laptop public keys, assemble one line from VM A's copied fields, no SSH comment and one space between fields:

walklaptop ssh-ed25519 <VM A-ssh-public-base64> <VM A-wireguard-public-key> 10.73.<n>.3

Use exactly the ssh_public_key and wireguard_public_key from VM A's Copy my public keys for walk6, and the host network <n> from step 2-3. Click Next, check Step 3 of 4 — Check and start and click Admit a project admin. Expected: (not run) walkadmin is admitted with walklaptop at 10.73.<n>.3; the Laptop retains its separate host-admin .2 peer. Failure signs: wrong public halves/address, whitespace/comment refusal or a host helper refusal.

On the Laptop, 4-3. Click Finish to close Admit a project admin (wizard-next). In your own account, in Claude Code, run the check for 6-host.md, host-person-admit:

Expected: (not run) walkadmin is admitted, walklaptop is VM A at 10.73.<n>.3, with its source-restricted SSH key and own VPN peer, SSH is source restricted, the peer and private token files exist; host-person-admit passed. Failure signs: any expected: / got: mismatch, a nonzero exit, or the named passed line missing. Record a finding by its step name; return to this panel afterward. On the Laptop, 5-1. In the interface: open walk6's menu (⋮) and click Register a project…. In Step 1 of 5 — Project name, type walk6-demo and click Next; in Step 2 of 5 — Project admin account, type walkadmin and click Next. Expected: (not run) the wizard Register a project advances to Step 3 of 5 — Project signing public key. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with Use a name starting with a lower-case letter….

On the Laptop, 5-2. In the interface (Step 3 of 5 — Project signing public key): paste walkadmin's sole project signing public line carried from VM A in step 0-6 (ssh-ed25519 <base64>, with no comment) into Project signing public key, click Next, check the summary on Step 4 of 5 — Check and start, and click Register a project.
